how_to_apply: Rules label; nothing here changes your analysis. This study was analysed outside Studio, so its wells cannot be left out here: open its file in Studio to leave wells out with a reason, or follow a call down to its wells in Trace.

pack.label: Research use only. Rules are lab-editable examples with sources; they are not clinical run-validity rules.
pack.name: research-default

sources.citation: Bustin SA, Ruijter JM, van den Hoff MJB, et al. MIQE 2.0: revision of the Minimum Information for Publication of Quantitative Real-Time PCR Experiments guidelines. Clin Chem 2025;71(6):634-651.

rules.statement: A plate with no wells typed as controls (no-template, no-RT, no-amplification, positive, standard) cannot be gated; it is shown as ungated, loudly, until its controls are typed.
rules.title: Typed controls on the plate

sources.citation: Bustin SA, Ruijter JM, van den Hoff MJB, et al. MIQE 2.0: revision of the Minimum Information for Publication of Quantitative Real-Time PCR Experiments guidelines. Clin Chem 2025;71(6):634-651.

rules.statement: When a negative control shows amplification, a study sample counts as positive only if its Cq precedes the earliest amplifying control's by at least k cycles; samples closer than that are flagged, with the share of their signal such contamination could contribute.
rules.title: No-template control amplification near the study samples

sources.citation: By analogy with clinical run-validity practice (e.g. the CDC 2019-nCoV RT-PCR panel instructions). Cited to explain the rule; research-default does not copy clinical rules.

rules.statement: Signal in a no-amplification control means the target's signal on this plate may not depend on amplification; every study well of that target on the plate is flagged.
rules.title: Amplification in a no-amplification control

sources.citation: Laurell H, Iacovoni JS, Abot A, et al. Correction of RT-qPCR data for genomic DNA-derived signals with ValidPrime. Nucleic Acids Res 2012;40(7):e51. Grade cut-offs applied here to a no-RT estimate (a qPilot adaptation, not the ValidPrime method).
Bustin SA, Ruijter JM, van den Hoff MJB, et al. MIQE 2.0: revision of the Minimum Information for Publication of Quantitative Real-Time PCR Experiments guidelines. Clin Chem 2025;71(6):634-651.

rules.statement: The genomic-DNA share of a sample's signal is estimated as E^-(Cq no-RT - Cq RT) and graded A (< 3 %), B (3-25 %), C (25-60 %) or F (> 60 %). No correction is applied.
rules.title: Genomic DNA share from the no-RT control

rules.statement: A positive control is checked against a Cq window the lab sets for that control; without a mapped control and window the rule is not applicable.
rules.title: Positive control inside its window

sources.citation: Ma H, Bell KN, Loker RN. qPCR and qRT-PCR analysis: regulatory points to consider when conducting biodistribution and vector shedding studies. Mol Ther Methods Clin Dev 2021;20:152-168 (Table 4).
Hellemans J, Vandesompele J, et al. PrimePCR assays: meeting the MIQE guidelines by full wet-lab validation. Bio-Rad Bulletin 6262 (efficiency 90-110 %).
Bio-Rad. Real-Time PCR Applications Guide, Bulletin 5279 (R2 > 0.980).
Bustin SA, Ruijter JM, van den Hoff MJB, et al. MIQE 2.0: revision of the Minimum Information for Publication of Quantitative Real-Time PCR Experiments guidelines. Clin Chem 2025;71(6):634-651.

rules.statement: Cq is regressed on log10 quantity over the amplified standard wells; efficiency 10^(-1/slope) with its 95 % confidence interval must fall inside the window and R2 above the minimum, with at least three levels. In relative quantification a failure does not taint study samples; it marks the curve as an efficiency source.
rules.title: Standard curve

sources.citation: Ruiz-Villalba A, Ruijter JM, van den Hoff MJB. Use and misuse of Cq in qPCR data analysis and reporting. Life 2021;11(6):496.
Bar T, Stahlberg A, Muszta A, Kubista M. Kinetic Outlier Detection (KOD) in real-time PCR. Nucleic Acids Res 2003;31(17):e105.

rules.statement: The Cq range of n replicate wells is compared with the 95th percentile of the range of n normal values whose SD combines pipetting (CV c) and Poisson sampling (1/N copies): sqrt(c^2 + 1/N) / ln(E). Copies come from a standard curve on the plate; without one, only pipetting counts up to Cq 30, a two-cycle floor applies up to Cq 35, and later groups are not evaluated. Outside the range is a warning; the consequence test decides.
rules.title: Technical replicate spread

sources.citation: Bustin S, Dhillon HS, Kirvell S, et al. Variability of the reverse transcription step: practical implications. Clin Chem 2015;61(1):202-212 (published online 2014).

rules.statement: Where the design marks reverse-transcription replicates (samples of one biological unit reverse-transcribed separately from the same RNA: the sample sheet's rt_replicate column), each replicate's Cq is the mean Cq of its study wells, and the range between the replicates of one unit and target must stay below the limit. A range at or above it is a warning; the consequence test decides. Without annotated replicates the rule is not applicable: the spread of reverse transcription is not measured.
rules.title: Reverse-transcription replicate spread

sources.citation: The instrument's own run file (a QuantStudio or StepOne .eds, a QuantStudio results export, CFX run information): the run state, the event log and each calibration's expiry as the vendor's software wrote them. qPilot reads them (methods/instrument_context.md) and adds no threshold of its own.

rules.statement: For each plate, its run file says whether the run completed, whether it was paused or a lid or drawer opened (and in which cycles), which calibrations were past the vendor's expiry at run time, and whether a hold drifted from its setpoint by more than the lab's limit. Each of these is a warning to weigh, not a reason to set the run aside: the consequence test says whether leaving the run's study wells out changes a call. The study's own file (RDML) names the instrument and the run date at most; a person links the instrument's run file to a plate to check the rest.
rules.title: What the run file says about the run

run_note: The study's own file (RDML) names the instrument and the run date at most. A study opened from an instrument export reads each plate's run file in the export when it has one (a QuantStudio results export, CFX run information). Link the run file the instrument wrote for a plate (an .eds file, a QuantStudio results export or CFX run information) and G-INSTR reads it instead: whether the run completed, its pauses and its calibrations. Linking changes no number; it is kept for every analysis of this file, with who linked it and when. Serial numbers in the file are never shown.
